terra.problem: The address joke makes the man's difficult living situation the punchline.
“Wrong place to look” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
The crowd of strong people and their long day are invented details, not facts the passage gives.
The line about Jesus not having said hello suggests He hasn't spoken yet, but He had already commanded the spirit to come out.
“Gets stoned” has a well-known second meaning.
The statement that Son of David is a title for Jesus needs a reference outside this passage.
The reason for the name Legion is given in verse 9, not the next verse.
The statement that Beelzebul appears elsewhere in the Gospels needs a reference.
The passage says they are many, not that many voices speak from the man.
“I'm only repeating what Mark gives us” comments on how Papa Dorin is telling the passage.
“The next stop” refers to the lesson's structure.
Saying they don't ask for anything else overlooks the repeated request not to be sent out of the region.
The line about the pigs not stopping is a flat, unhelpful observation.
The cookie-sheet comparison doesn't make clear sense as a measure of a herd of animals.
The selected word completes “two hundred,” but the explanation compares the herd with one hundred.
The cookie-sheet joke makes it sound as though a dozen pigs would fit on one sheet, so the comparison doesn't work.
“I won't make one up” comments on Papa Dorin's storytelling approach.
“I'll leave it there” comments on how Papa Dorin is telling the passage.
Jesus says “your own people”; the passage does not identify them specifically as the man's family.
